_comments: ORDER HEADERS IS A LAYERED BASE VIEW.
CodeGen keeps writing the whole generated view — 13 display joins, a geo join keyed by a
hardcoded entity GUID, an OUTER APPLY to a generated root-ID function — under the INNER name
below. This app then owns a four-line wrapper that selects `g.*` and adds `IsOverdue`.
WHY NOT A COMPUTED COLUMN. The predicate needs GETUTCDATE(), and PostgreSQL generated columns
must be immutable — so it would work on SQL Server and fail to port, which is exactly what D41
ruled out when it chose trigger-maintained rollups for cross-platform parity. Layering is
SQL Server only (MJ refuses it on PG rather than shipping a documented footgun), so the PG side
keeps deriving IsOverdue in code from the same shared rule.
WHY NOT A FULLY CUSTOM VIEW. BaseViewGenerated = 0 with no GeneratedBaseViewName makes CodeGen
stop generating entirely — this app would inherit all 81 lines and hand-maintain them forever,
and a foreign key added later would silently never get its display field.
⚠️ ADOPTING THIS ON AN EXISTING ENTITY NEEDS A SCOPED forceRegeneration. Setting
GeneratedBaseViewName is a METADATA change, so the entity never lands in CodeGen's
modified/new list, and logSQLForNewOrModifiedEntity only writes migration output for entities
in that list. CodeGen WILL create the inner view in whatever database you ran it against and
emit NOTHING — your box looks right while every other environment never receives the view, and
